outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: repair_asides now settles each recorded move through _settle_move, classified by git's record of the tree (the admin dir the move recorded, the tree its gitdir names via _record_names, the marker and the lock in it via _lock_reason), never by which directory stands. No admin dir -> _forget_move with a did-line, never a stop (p3). Record names `from` and `from` holds it -> take back, but only when the marker names the set-aside key or the lock is the drive's; a tree cut there since (git reuses a pruned record's dir name, verified with git 2.53.0) is left alone (p4 and its reused-name variant). Record names `from` or the aside and the aside holds it -> repair. Otherwise the tree is missing: only a record under the drive's own ASIDE_LOCK stops (aside_missing), naming `git worktree repair <from>` when the tree is back at `from` (p2) or `git worktree unlock <path>` + `git worktree prune`; any other record is forgotten. (a) _take_back_aside drops the entries only once marker and unlock both held; otherwise the move stays recorded and the next step retries. (b) _repoint_module writes the absolute path when os.path.relpath raises ValueError across drives; _repair_moved_tree/_finish_aside now return (step, why) and aside_unread picks the remedy per step from ASIDE_REMEDY (repair, repoint, read-back, unlock). (c) _git_floor asks `git --version` before set_aside_tree records/locks/moves anything; below 2.30 the redo stops. audit-status.py: kept_trees_block takes the loaded manifest and gives each tree a remedy (_kept_tree_remedy): task-remove for a plan task, `/audit:phase <phase>` while asideMoves still records it, else `git worktree remove <path>`; _kept_tree_lines prints it on the row. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the set-aside paragraph rewritten for the classification, the per-step remedy, the git floor, the absolute repoint and the status remedy; ta13b reference replaced. Tests: ta13 updated to the (step, why) contract; ta13b (cross-drive was a reason) replaced by ta18 (absolute path); new ta15, ta15b, ta16, ta16b, ta17, ta18, ta18b, ta18c, ta19 in _aside_record_cases; kt5, kt5b in test_audit_status. outcome.descriptive: A recorded set-aside move is now settled by git's own record, so a deleted aside or record no longer wedges the drive, a new tree at the task path is never taken back, and every stop names a command that acts.

testsAdded: ta15: a move whose record and aside a human removed is forgotten with a did-line, no step stops
ta15b: a live drive-locked record whose tree is gone stops, and its unlock+prune remedy runs and the next step goes on
ta16: a new tree cut at the task path over a half-held move keeps its marker base; the stop names the unlock
ta16b: a new tree given the pruned record's directory name is not taken back
ta17: a take-back whose unlock fails keeps the move recorded; the next step unlocks it
ta18: a cross-drive submodule repoint writes an absolute core.worktree
ta18b/ta18c: a repoint or read-back failure stops naming that step, not git worktree repair
ta19: git older than 2.30 refuses the set-aside before the rename
kt5/kt5b: status names git worktree remove for a set-aside tree, task-remove for a task, the drive's next step for an unfinished move
